items.title: AI as a helper: a tip for new freelancers
items.pt:
AI tools are not a replacement for your abilities; they are a strong helper.


Michael C. Clark, The Freelancer's Playbook (Secret 10: Scaling Your Earnings with Automation & AI)

items.title: After every paycheck, see what's left
items.pt:
Monthly budgets assume one paycheck and a calm week. A lot of people get paid twice a month, or weekly, and the money is gone before the spreadsheet catches up.

A simpler rule: start from this paycheck. Subtract the bills that come out of it, what you already spent since that payday, debt payments, and anything you meant to save. The leftover is the only number that matters until the next payday.

items.title: Less Decoder is More Encoder: Geometric Representation Learning from Novel View Synthesis
items.pt: This paper examines the role of Novel View Synthesis (NVS) in geometric representation learning. In principle, NVS should reason about 3D scene structure, thereby enabling transferable multi-view geometric representations. Yet, existing encoder-based NVS methods yield poor representations. This is not because of a lack of supervisory signal, but rather due to inconspicuous architectural choices: \textit{spatially expressive decoders} that dilute representational capabilities of the scene encoder

items.title: MoSE3: Learning World-Space SE(3) at Every Pixel
items.pt: Dense 3D point tracking has been a prominent paradigm for modeling motion in dynamic scenes, but a point track is just a 3-DoF translation curve per pixel: it captures where pixels go, not the rotation of the underlying part, nor which pixels move together as one body. We propose MoSE3, the first feed-forward model that predicts dense SE(3) motion from monocular RGB video, producing full 6-DoF rigid transforms at every pixel in world space. items.title: 4DCodeBench: Benchmarking Agents on Inverse Graphics of Dynamic Scenes
items.pt: We introduce 4DCodeBench, a benchmark for 4D inverse graphics through code generation, in which agents reconstruct dynamic scenes from video as executable graphics programs. items.title: What Should World Models Forget? Stratified Retention for Continual Adaptation
items.pt: Continual learning treats degradation on previously seen data as evidence of failure, a convention inherited from settings with a stationary prediction target, where a correct label remains correct indefinitely. World models do not satisfy this condition. Their prediction target is the environment, which changes, so knowledge that was accurate when acquired may later become false, and discarding it is required behavior rather than a defect.
